courses.description: Investigations into the intrinsic meaning of the site will be coupled with the effective channeling of those issues into the work of art. Ideas, material, and placement will be analyzed so as to achieve cogent integration into the site. Introduction to use of scale models and various types of models to analyze a site and plan work for a site is part of this course. Lectures, individual discussions, and group critiques are scheduled.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in (( FDPR 1531 and FDPR 1532 ) or VS 1351 ) and ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Mold Making Technology
courses.description: Flexible moldmaking techniques are explored using foam, latex, RTV and silicone rubber, as well as alginate compounds for direct body casts. Non-flexible techniques include wood forms for cement castings. Positives are cast in cement, plaster, rubber and polyurethane using both solid and hollow casting methods. Students incorporate these techniques in directed projects, or for completing self-directed work.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in (( FDPR 1531 and FDPR 1532 ) or VS 1351 ) and ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Figure Modeling
courses.description: This course stresses clinical observation as well as analytical response to issues pertaining to the body. The nature and aspects of representation in the sculptural tradition are considered. Work from the model in class.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in (( FDPR 1511 and FDPR 1512 ) or VS 1351 )

courses.title: Sculpture: Rome
courses.description: This is an introductory course on the basic principles of object making. Demos on specific material use and procedures will alternate with lectures and site visits that will link the course with the student's experience of Italian art and architecture. Working with a variety of methods and materials including plaster casting, clay and wax modeling and concrete fabricating process, students will learn to communicate technically as well as conceptually through three-dimensional form.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in (( FDPR 1511 and FDPR 1512 ) or VS 1351 )

courses.title: Figure Modeling: Rome
courses.description: This course focuses entirely on the human figure as subject. Along with working from the model in class there will be visits to museums and sculptural sites introducing students to the figurative tradition in Rome: artwork ranging from ancient Greek and Roman carvings to Baroque figures in movement that characterize the cityscape. While the course is designed to help the student develop an understanding of the artistic representation of the human figure in historic and aesthetic terms, its ultimate goal is to have each student develop a personal interpretation of figuration as it relates to contemporary culture.

courses.title: Sculpture Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics in sculpture.

courses.title: Social Practice and Socially Engaged Art
courses.description: This course introduces students to the many issues and ideas in Social Practice and Socially Engaged Art practices. These disciplines build on a lineage of contemporary art movements including public art, institutional critique, performance art, relational aesthetics, guerilla art and environmental art. We will investigate the role of accessibility, audience, participation, permanence, community, ownership, interactivity and politics in public works. The focus will be to create socially motivated and participatory art that engages non-art audiences and that exists outside of traditional art venues. This engagement with varying audiences, from passersby to targeted participants will take different forms, including collaborations, the creation of new experiences in familiar and known sites (i.e. Temple campus), the provision "services" in unexpected locations, the activation of historical sites and monuments, and the repurposing of unused and under-used locations around North Philadelphia and the city.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1511 (may be taken concurrently) or FDPR 1512 (may be taken concurrently)) and FDPR 1531 .

courses.title: Honors Special Topics
courses.description: In this studio art course, approaches to making and understanding images in various media will be addressed.

courses.title: Honors Digital Imaging: Seeing Photographically
courses.description: Life is full of wonder when you simply open your eyes to it. All it takes is an open mind and a shift in your way of seeing. The primary objective of this course is to introduce students to the act of seeing photographically, creative problem solving, and thinking visually while learning contemporary digital technology and practices. Students will be instructed on the use of a variety of input and output devices (cameras, scanners, printers) and software applications. Lecture and research on historical and contemporary artwork inform creative approaches to visual thinking and assignments build on creative problem-solving skill sets. Emphasis is placed on image making, proper workflow, interpretation, and output. Students produce a portfolio that demonstrates critical visual thinking and effective skill development.

courses.title: Special Topics in Art
courses.description: In this studio art course, approaches to making and understanding images, objects and experiences in various media will be addressed. Each topic will be addressed through contextual, procedural, material and critical lenses. This course assumes a strong level of basic studio knowledge in one or more art disciplines.

courses.title: Interactive Projects
courses.description: The intent of this course is to broaden the studio practice through the use of interactive technologies. Students will create a portfolio web site and an animated, interactive Flash project to be shown on the web or CD-ROM. Software explored in this course includes DreamWeaver, Flash and SoundEdit 16. Basic HTML and Action Scripting is also included in the curriculum. The finished work will be burned onto a CD-ROM and posted on the web. NOTE: Special Authorization for Non-Majors.

courses.title: 3D Product Design and Animation
courses.description: Integrating the fundamentals of 3D design across the disciplines of graphic design, interactive design, and illustration, this course equips students with the skills to create immersive, three-dimensional visuals that transcend traditional boundaries. Engaging with advanced 3D modeling, texturing, and rendering techniques, participants from diverse creative backgrounds will explore how 3D design can amplify the impact of their work, whether in storytelling, brand development, or digital experiences. The curriculum, grounded in hands-on learning through industry-standard software, encourages exploration and innovation, allowing students to bring their unique visions to life in a 3D space. This course is designed not only to broaden the technical toolkit of designers and illustrators but also to foster a deep understanding of how 3D elements can enhance visual communication in a variety of media.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in DES 2002 .

courses.title: Core 2: Research, Practice, Agency
courses.description: In this course, students will engage as artists in contemporary issues, problems, and needs of everyday life. Students will work collaboratively and collectively, sharing skills. This class is a seminar and a workshop/laboratory, meaning that issues/problems/needs will be addressed and worked through via research and making; discussion and production; theory and practice. Students learn to map, navigate, and intervene in the material and immaterial media, networks, and infrastructures that determine perception, knowledge, and experience. Modeling different artistic-productive practices will empower students to think and act beyond existing categories and narratives of what it means to be a creative subject in the world. This course is as much about the critical-thoughtful assessment of given perspectives and circumstances and the attitudes, technologies, and methods that begets them, as it encourages their transformation. Students learn how to increase their impact as individual makers as they expand upon given and latent notions of authorship, production, function, participation, and audience. The focus of the class is to produce propositions and models as speculative-pragmatic outcomes, asking artists to creatively engage in the world by offering ways to see, sense, map, interact, and work that critically forge new processes and forms of being and becoming, offering alternative pasts, presents, and futures.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2052 .

courses.title: Virtual Worlds: Creative Computing
courses.description: How does virtual space change our perception of time, movement, and objects? This course introduces art students to virtual reality (VR) as an expressive medium. Students will explore the artistic potential of VR and coding using VR drawing tools, game design software and AI-assisted coding. Over the course of the semester students will create immersive, interactive VR artworks of their own design. Students will acquire an advanced set of applied skills covering the workflows that support VR technologies and creative coding practices, moving from idea to finalized artwork. Students will interrogate the ethical and artistic potential of VR to develop innovative, creative projects that deepen and broaden their vocabulary as artists, while learning a sense of critical awareness of their digital heritage.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2063 , ART 1402 , or ART 2402 )

courses.title: Immersive Spaces: Interactive Technologies
courses.description: What happens when a viewer becomes a protagonist in a scene, transforming the passive experience of viewing art into active engagement? Today's technologies enable new modes of creation and viewer experience. In this class, students produce multimedia works that encompass immersive video and sound, Augmented Reality, and projection mapping. We explore how artificial intelligence (AI) technologies can be a collaborative tool. This course introduces students to a range of computational and programming software as tools for creative practice and as opportunities for viewer immersion and participation.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2062 or ART 2063 )

courses.title: Time and Technology in Contemporary Art Practices
courses.description: What are the urgent issues circulating through contemporary time-based and digital, new media artworks? This seminar introduces art practices and theory that interrogate time and technology as conceptual strategies for creative work. The ethics, attitudes, and politics of today's technology shape our society; and art practices that use technology often do so to critique or reconfigure our society. The study of alternate models of time (e.g. non-linear, synchronous, queer, cyclical) provide terminology to analyze time-based practices in performance, installation, and video to, for example, analyze how time may be manipulated to create alternative conceptions of society. Module topics are: Time and Temporality; Digital Technologies in Art; Ethics and Critique; Audience and Performance; and Conceptual Strategies. Course content is delivered through readings, presentations, and assignments that allow participants to deepen their knowledge of the ways time and technology inform, shape, and impact our understanding of society, culture, and the environment. Field trips and visiting artist talks enrich direct engagement with the course material.

courses.title: Field Internship
courses.description: A field internship must provide practical experience in a setting which is relevant to the student's course of study, such as in a gallery, museum or community art center, etc. A comprehensive paper must be written.

courses.title: Advanced Ceramics I
courses.description: Problems in ceramics for the advanced student with emphasis on individual research projects and upon portfolio development.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Two-Dimensional Ceramics
courses.description: The making and production of tiles and other essentially two-dimensional ceramic items for application to interior and exterior architecture. Several processes, techniques and firing methods are explored. These include both high and low temperature firing, mold, and hand pressing techniques. The history of tiles and ceramic wall reliefs are surveyed with concentration on relevant periods and countries.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Ceramic Materials
courses.description: An advanced level examination of ceramic processes, the formulation of clay bodies and glazes, common firing practices, and the construction of kilns. NOTE: The course required and intended for ceramic majors.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Porcelain
courses.description: A ceramic course that covers the special properties of porcelain clay. Various hand building, throwing and casting techniques are explored as well as experiments in glazing and the preparation of clay bodies. Historical importance of porcelain is reviewed along with many contemporary uses of this material in vessel and sculptural forms.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Advanced Throwing and Wheel Work
courses.description: A course concentrating on the use of the potter's wheel, using a problem-solving approach. Structured to develop the necessary skills to enable the student in making personal aesthetic choices with regard to three-dimensional ceramic forms created on the wheel.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Ceramic Mold Making
courses.description: Students produce both two and three-piece plaster molds to be used in the slip casting process for the production of multiple ceramic items. The course examines both the historical and contemporary use of molds and slip casting. During the semester the students are encouraged to incorporate the use of slip casting into their current style of work.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 .

courses.title: Ceramic Structures
courses.description: The approach to this course is to utilize ceramic materials for the creation of sculpture. The history of ceramic sculpture as well as contemporary movements is stressed. Various techniques used in ceramic sculpture, techniques and materials used in conjunction with ceramics are explored.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Ceramic Workshop
courses.description: Ceramic Workshop is a course where a variety of skill levels and aesthetic points of view can interact. The course itself rotates through several specialty topics corresponding to current themes in Ceramics.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2102 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Threading the Needle: Drawing with Stitch
courses.description: This course focuses on stitch as a form of mark making, exploring surface applications such as embroidery, beading, collage, transfers and forms of layering through additive and subtractive processes. Using conventional and unconventional substrates students will explore the power of mark making as a form of disruption. Readings, lectures and critiques contribute to the development of conceptual concerns and provide knowledge of historical work and contemporary artistic practices.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2201 and ART 2202 .

courses.title: Soft Sculpture
courses.description: This course examines the transformation of traditional and nontraditional materials to three-dimensional forms, surfaces, and spaces. The exploration of pliable materials will be realized through hand and machine stitching, mark making, embellishment, felting, stuffing, and manipulation of armature. Students are encouraged to develop a personal direction in soft sculptural practice, with emphasis on material investigation and research. Individual and group critiques and discussion of both historic and contemporary artists and concepts augment the course.

courses.title: Alternative Materials II
courses.description: This class allows students to further develop their work and research in this area and introduce intermediate and more advanced techniques; working more independently students are able to pursue specific areas projects, developing their skills learned in Alternative Materials I.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2203 .

courses.title: Weaving II
courses.description: Exploration of dyeing and printing including space dyed ikat and printing on the woven surface. Prior to Fall 2025, the course title was "Woven Structure II."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2204 .

courses.title: Experimental Costume
courses.description: This course is the exploration of the histories and techniques involved in the construction of clothing, costume, fashion, and haute couture. The term clothing implies protection against the elements and to preserve modesty. Costume functions beyond simple utility, becoming a means of seduction by enhancing nature, or adding artificial attraction. Fashion and haute couture indulge the fantasy of the creator. Students will be encouraged to explore their own interpretations of these terms through construction: machine knitting, crochet, hand and machine sewing, and embroidery. Students may also experiment with documentation methods, including performance, fashion shows, photography, and video as media to exhibit cumulated work. Note: Prior to Fall 2024 this course was titled "Figurative Futures - Technology and the Body" and prior to Fall 2023 this course was titled "Body Art and Adornment."

courses.title: Sewn
courses.description: Sewn construction will be the focus of this class. Students will work with a myriad of sewing technologies including but not limited to the long arm sewing machine, industrial sergers and domestic machines and hand sewing. The focus is on manipulating pliable elements to create structure and form. This class will be augmented with readings, field trips, lectures and visiting artists.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1531 , FDPR 1532 , or VS 1351 )

courses.title: Intermediate Fibers and Material Studies
courses.description: Intermediate Fibers and Material Studies allows students an opportunity to further develop their work and research through introducing intermediate and more advanced techniques; working independently students are able to pursue specific areas and projects.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2201 or ART 2202 )

courses.title: Jacquard
courses.description: The Jacquard loom interfaces with a computer allowing for control of each thread. This allows for a multitude of possibilities. Students explore the Jacquard while also learning about its history and relationship to punched card systems and early computers. Working with digital sources and alternative materials students will create woven works. The class will include weaving, working on a computer, readings, lectures, writing and field trips.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2204 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.title: Screen Print on Fabric
courses.description: Screen-printing is a versatile printmaking technique that allows reproduction of an image and/or a repetition of an image. Students will be introduced to a vast array of processes including but not limited to silkscreen, digital printing, heat transfer, mono printing, stencil, stamp printing and block printing. The emphasis will be placed on conceptual development of language and using print in a contemporary art context. Final projects may take the form of installation, soft sculptures, yardage or site specific work.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1521 , FDPR 1522 , or VS 1151 )

courses.title: Special Topics in Fibers and Material Studies
courses.description: This course varies from semester to semester; the class content responds to current themes in Fibers and Material Studies and the varying discourses associated. Special topics classes typically include studio work, readings, lectures, writing and field trips.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1521 , FDPR 1522 , FDPR 1531 , or FDPR 1532 )

courses.title: Cultivating a Collection
courses.description: Through in-depth textile research and learned construction techniques, students will create a collection to be exhibited in the annual show. Visiting artists, independent studio time and critique will support the cumulative collection. At the end of the semester, students will debut their collection in the annual Wearable Art Show.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2201 .

courses.title: Digital Drawing and Pattern Making
courses.description: Using the digital hand, students will design one-of-a-kind garments to be printed and constructed to make unique wearables. Students will have first-hand experience and participate in the industry standard in pattern drafting and construction. Students will utilize Adobe Suite and a large format fabric printer.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2201 .

courses.title: Experimental Costume and Performance
courses.description: This class will explore garment construction through a performance lens, looking at artists who create silhouette extension or body distortion through both movement and pattern making. Students will learn necessary sewing skills and garment manipulation to facilitate performative workshops throughout the class.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2201 .

courses.title: History of Wearable Art and Costume
courses.description: Through independent research, readings, and discussion, students will examine the extensive history of wearable art and garment. Introductions to the cultural, political, historical, and aesthetic dimensions of experimental costume will focus on examination in relation to contemporary art.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2201 .

courses.title: Dyeing for Color II
courses.description: This class allows students to further develop their work and research in dyeing and related processes through introducing intermediate and more advanced techniques; working independently students are able to pursue specific areas and projects.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2202 .

courses.title: Hot Glass, Topic: Blowing
courses.description: A glass course primarily for the glass major who wants to learn advanced skills in off-hand techniques for blowing traditional and non-traditional glass forms. Advanced color work, team work and advanced methods for combining complicated glass forms will be a major component of this studio class. NOTE: Six hours of studio work outside of class time is required.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 and ART 2302 .

courses.title: Glass Construction, Topic: Kiln Working
courses.description: Predominantly a course in glass object-making. This class will provide beginning instruction through advanced tutelage in kiln forming techniques. Traditional and contemporary processes covered include frit casting from both clay and wax positives, fusing, and slumping. Moldmaking is emphasized and a variety of refractory mold materials will be introduced. A repertoire of finishing processes will be offered to aid in taking the kiln worked object to its completed state.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1531 , FDPR 1532 , or VS 1351 )

courses.title: Glass Construction, Topic: Cold Glass
courses.description: This studio course provides comprehensive instruction with regard to "cold" glass-working techniques. 2-D and 3-D glass objects will be constructed with the employment of a variety of procedures without the introduction of heat. The classes will encourage the areas of student expertise. Thus, information on surface treatment (glass texturing), joining (glass to glass, to other materials), and finishing processes will be covered. Proficiency in the creation of structurally and conceptually cohesive objects is stressed.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 and ART 2302 .

courses.title: Glass Workshop
courses.description: An intensive daily studio course designed for beginning students through advanced glass majors. This studio course meets each day. Studio demonstrations in all hot glass applications are the focus. Individual problem solving through guided team work will be emphasized. NOTE: Three hours of studio work outside of class each day is required.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 .

courses.title: Hot Glass Casting
courses.description: A glass class that will provide beginning advanced instruction on using molten glass as a material for casting into a wide variety of mold materials. Methods of mold setup, methods for pouring hot glass and finishing glass will be provided and demonstrated. A survey of contemporary craft-artists using these materials and methods will be shown. Presentation and evaluation of finished work will be an important aspect of this studio course.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1531 , FDPR 1532 , or VS 1351 )

courses.title: Advanced Glass Seminar
courses.description: This studio course is for the junior glass major. The emphasis is on historical glass research topics. A survey of glass making from ancient cultures to early American glass will be covered by slide lectures, museum visits, and research projects.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 and ART 2302 .

courses.title: Advanced Glass, Topic: Visiting Artist Series
courses.description: This course is for the junior glass major.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 and ART 2302 .

courses.title: Glass in an Expanded Field
courses.description: This course is a core studio experience for glass majors and is also open to students interested in incorporating glass into their practice. It offers an interdisciplinary exploration of glass, emphasizing how the material functions within a broader ecological, conceptual, and artistic context. Students will develop a personal language through glass and other media, while investigating sustainable practices, responsible sourcing of materials, and innovative approaches to working with glass. The course encourages students to expand beyond traditional glass techniques, considering glass as part of a larger ecosystem. Through hands-on projects, research, and fieldwork, students will explore the role of glass in various industries, artistic practices, and contemporary culture. They will engage with the environmental impact of glass production, identify unique ways of utilizing the material, and respond to contemporary glass practices with critical inquiry and creativity.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 .

courses.title: Special Topics in Glass
courses.description: Selected topics in glass. Each topic will be addressed through contextual, procedural, material and critical lenses.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1521 , FDPR 1522 , FDPR 1531 , or FDPR 1532 )

courses.title: Neon
courses.description: Throughout this course, we will learn about the applications of light and neon in contemporary art and the technical skills required to make our own signs. We will demonstrate and practice bending glass tubes, making patterns, wiring, mounting and displaying finished work. While we will start off with learning basic skills, as the semester progresses our focus will be on incorporating neon into an existing or new studio practice and pushing the boundaries of what the medium can do conceptually.

courses.title: Stained Glass
courses.description: Students in this course will learn how to design and create stained glass windows. The course will cover copper foil and soldering techniques, traditional painting on glass, and sandblasting imagery onto glass to include in the students designs.

courses.title: Flameworking
courses.description: In this flameworking course, students will learn to manipulate glass rods and tubes using torches, exploring fundamental skills such as shaping, bending, and joining to create unique forms and objects. Throughout the course, emphasis will be placed on technical proficiency, material understanding, and personal expression. Students will gain experience in a range of flameworking methods, including solid sculpting, hollow forms, and mixed-media integration. Projects will encourage experimentation with scale, texture, and surface finishes to develop individual artistic voices. Through demonstrations, hands-on practice, and critiques, students will deepen their understanding of flameworking as both a craft and an art form. Historical and contemporary contexts will be explored to inspire conceptual thinking and innovative approaches.

courses.title: Moldmaking: Hot
courses.description: A glass course primarily for the glass major who wants to learn advanced skills in off-hand techniques for blowing traditional and non-traditional glass forms. Advanced color work, team work and advanced methods for combining complicated glass forms will be a major component of this studio class. NOTE: Six hours of studio work outside of class time is required.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 .

courses.title: Crafting Empathy
courses.description: This course delves into the transformative power of artmaking, focusing specifically on the collaborative and empathetic aspects inherent in the process of glassmaking. Students will explore how artists leverage the act of creating to positively impact physical, mental, and emotional well-being, both for themselves and their communities. By examining arts organizations that integrate making as a theoretical framework or community-building tool, students will gain insights into the broader societal implications of creative practices. Through hands-on experiences in the studio, participants will engage in various forms of collaborative making, utilizing hot glass and flameworking techniques to foster empathy, compassion, and a deeper understanding of the impact art can have on personal and collective well-being.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 .

courses.title: Glass Color Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive study of the technical and theoretical applications of color in hot glassmaking, with an emphasis on sustainable and eco-conscious production methods. Through three progressive projects, students will develop their skills in color making, material production, and integrating hybrid techniques into their artistic practice. Collaborative and individual projects will deepen students' understanding of glass chemistry, historical and contemporary uses of color, and the transformative properties of the medium.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2301 .

courses.title: Metals Workshop
courses.description: Summer classes for variable credit in specialized subjects: advanced fabrication, mechanisms, machine tool processes, advanced lapidary and stone setting, linkages and advanced casting. Students have the opportunity to learn and utilize specialized technologies. It is also an opportunity to complete projects or participate in a class designed for students who studied abroad. This class requires special permission from the instructor.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2401 .

courses.title: CAD-CAM I: Introduction to 3D Modeling
courses.description: In this introduction to CAD-CAM, the students learn to: customize the modeling environment; create basic graphic objects-lines, circles, arcs, curves, solids and surfaces; draw with precision; create, test and verify solid models in STL file format for production of rapid prototypes and render models. Students will learn to use professional-level software used for 3D modeling across many industries worldwide, including product design, architecture and jewelry. Students follow self-guided lessons/assignments to learn the basics of computer aided design (CAD), then use the digital tools learned in creating original projects. Generally, one session per week will be devoted to demonstrating the lessons and related CAD functionality, and the second session will be devoted to independent projects and scheduled one-on-one time with the instructor. This 3000-level course is offered for graduate and upper-level undergraduate students. NOTE: This course is sometimes offered as an online course under Section Number 701. Prior to Fall 2023 this course was titled "CAD/CAM I Computer-Aided-Design/Computer-Aided-Manufacture."

courses.title: CAD-CAM II: Intermediate 3D Modeling
courses.description: In this continuation from CAD-CAM I ( ART 2402 ), students will continue learning computer aided design (CAD) software to create basic objects and 3D models for the production of rapid prototypes (3D printing); and rendering. CAD will supplement bench-based making techniques, such as casting and cold connections. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to use software to create three-dimensional models for virtual reality, rapid prototyping via 3D printing, patterns for use in bench work, and photorealistic rendering. The course will discuss and experiment with a multitude of materials, from wax to porcelain. This 3000-level course is offered for graduate and upper-level undergraduate students. Prior to Fall 2023 this course was titled "CAD/CAM II Computer-Aided-Design/Computer-Aided-Manufacture."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2402 or ART 3402 )

courses.title: Advanced 3D Modeling
courses.description: This course is a continuation of Intermediate 3D Modeling. Students will be encouraged to produce Three-D CAD models for rapid prototyping and photo-realistic rendering.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2404 or ART 3404 )

courses.title: Intermediate Jewelry and Metals I
courses.description: Advanced problems exploring the design and fabrication of functional objects and jewelry. Three-dimensional sheet metal development, fabrication of hollow structures, mechanisms, linkage systems and mold making will be introduced. NOTE: This course is for majors only. Prior to Fall 2025, this course was titled "Junior Metalsmithing."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2401 or ART 1401 )

courses.title: Intermediate Jewelry and Metals II
courses.description: Advanced problems exploring the design and fabrication of functional objects and jewelry. Three-dimensional sheet metal development, fabrication of hollow structures, mechanisms, linkage systems and mold making will be introduced. NOTE: This course is for majors only. Prior to Fall 2025, this course was titled "Junior Metalsmithing."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 3406 .

courses.title: Electroforming Workshop
courses.description: Students with prior metalworking experience have the opportunity to explore nontraditional electrochemical processes for the creation of unique forms in metal.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2401 .

courses.title: Plastics for Jewelry and Objects
courses.description: An introduction to forming, fabricating, joining, and casting a variety of plastic materials. This 20th and 21st century material is studied for its visual and artistic potential, as well as its applications in product design. Students learn to combine these materials with metals and other media.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2401 or CRFT 2453 )

courses.title: Production Processes
courses.description: Introduction to production processes and marketing. Students will design and produce an object in quantity and be assisted in the marketing of that object.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2401 or CRFT 2453 )

courses.title: Color in Metals
courses.description: Aspects of applying color to metals or changing the existing color of metallic surfaces are explored. Students are introduced to the new techniques, color anodizing aluminum, and the space-age metals titanium and niobium. Application of color resin and vitreous enamels are also examined.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2401 or CRFT 2453 )

courses.title: Enameling
courses.description: All basic enameling techniques, which include Plique A Jour, Limoges, Champeleve, Bustail, etc. The course explores the use of synthetic resins as an addition to the enamelist's repertoire.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2401 or CRFT 2453 )

courses.title: Plastics for Jewelry
courses.description: Introduction to the forming, fabricating, and casting of plastic materials. The student works with acrylics, polyesters, urethanes, epoxies, and silicones, and learns to combine these materials with metal. NOTE: This course is for majors only. Metals/Jewelry/CAD-CAM Major.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2401 .

courses.title: Lapidary and Stone Setting
courses.description: Advanced lapidary processes are demonstrated which include the cutting and polishing of faceted stones designed by the student. Traditional and innovative stone setting methods are also explored.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2401 .

courses.title: Photo Processes and Etching Jewelry
courses.description: All aspects of the photographic processes that can be used with metals and plastics are introduced. This includes photo-resist techniques for metal etching, plating, and anodizing, along with photo embedments in plastics. NOTE: This course is for majors only.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2401 .

courses.title: Metalsmithing
courses.description: Advanced metal forming techniques are explored. Students are encouraged to produce functional hollowware and objects of a non-traditional source.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2401 or CRFT 2453 )

courses.title: Advanced Painting
courses.description: A studio painting course with emphasis on the development of a student's individual point of view. Class work focuses on the development of the student's ability to work at a conceptually advanced level. Experimentation is encouraged and there are frequent class critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Advanced Painting
courses.description: A studio painting course with emphasis on the development of a student's individual point of view. Class work focuses on the development of the student's ability to work at a conceptually advanced level. Experimentation is encouraged and there are frequent class critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Landscape
courses.description: An examination of painting problems involved in the variable light, space, and form of cityscape and landscape. Work from various sites and sources. NOTE: This course may fulfill an advanced Painting/Drawing Studio Major or Studio Elective.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Figure Painting
courses.description: A painting course based on direct observation. Fundamentals of oil painting as well as an understanding of anatomy, composition, and the relationship of the figure to its environment are stressed. The development of an individualized approach and the use of content are explored through group discussion and assigned work.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Color
courses.description: The study of color, its characteristics, and interaction, explored through studio painting experiences. NOTE: This course may fulfill an advanced Painting/Drawing Studio Major or Studio Elective.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Color
courses.description: The study of color, its characteristics, and interaction, explored through studio painting experiences. NOTE: This course may fulfill an advanced Painting/Drawing Studio Major or Studio Elective.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( PDS 2011 , PDS 2111 , ART 2501 , or ART 2503 ) and ( PDS 2311 , PDS 2321 , PDS 2331 , ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , ART 2508 , or PDS 2341 )

courses.title: Painting on Paper
courses.description: A study of the uses of aqueous media beyond transparent watercolor. Opaque watercolor, collage, and transfer techniques, and oil and acrylic on paper are explored.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( PDS 2011 , PDS 2111 , ART 2501 , or ART 2503 ) and ( PDS 2311 , PDS 2321 , PDS 2331 , ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , ART 2508 , or PDS 2341 )

courses.title: Painting on Paper
courses.description: A study of the uses of aqueous media beyond transparent watercolor. Opaque watercolor, collage, and transfer techniques, and oil and acrylic on paper are explored.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( PDS 2011 , PDS 2111 , ART 2501 , or ART 2503 ) and ( PDS 2311 , PDS 2321 , PDS 2331 , ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , ART 2508 , or PDS 2341 )

courses.title: Painting Workshop
courses.description: A studio painting course with emphasis on the development of a student's individual point of view. Class work will focus on the development of the student's ability to work at a conceptually advanced level. Experimentation is encouraged.

courses.title: Digital Drawing
courses.description: This course engages students with the possibilities of the computer as a drawing tool. Digital Drawing expands the conceptual and pictorial fundamentals of drawing and painting.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in (( FDPR 1511 and FDPR 1512 ) or VS 1151 )

courses.title: Rome Sketchbook
courses.description: Participants record their observations in sketchbook form on daily outings to significant sites. Rome - incomparably rich historically and visually - provides a host of subjects ideal for improving drawing technique. The concentration required in drawing directly from observation leads to a deeper understanding of the city's forms.

courses.title: Drawing Workshop
courses.description: Studies in drawing emphasizing individual instruction for students of varied backgrounds.

courses.title: Advanced Drawing
courses.description: In this studio-intensive course students engage in an investigation of subject matter, sources, and strategies for generating work. Experimentation is encouraged and there are frequent class critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Advanced Drawing: Rome
courses.description: This course combines studio work with the Rome experience as a way to explore ideas and materials as well as the development of an individualized approach to drawing. The goal of this studio course is not only to improve one's technical ability but to probe the limits of what can be done in drawing; defining the boundaries of what a drawing is, and how it relates to contemporary art and other studio practices.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( PDS 2311 , ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , PDS 2321 , or PDS 2331 )

courses.title: Advanced Drawing
courses.description: In this studio-intensive course students engage in an investigation of subject matter, sources, and strategies for generating work. Experimentation is encouraged and there are frequent class critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Figure Drawing
courses.description: An advanced course focused entirely on the human figure as subject. There is emphasis on a variety of approaches to drawing the figure. Dynamics, proportion, anatomy, volume, and structure will be investigated through various drawing methods and selected materials. Frequent historical references will be made through reproductions and slides, and 20th century figure drawing will be thoroughly discussed.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Figure Drawing
courses.description: An advanced course focused entirely on the human figure as subject. There is emphasis on a variety of approaches to drawing the figure. Dynamics, proportion, anatomy, volume, and structure will be investigated through various drawing methods and selected materials. Frequent historical references will be made through reproductions and slides, and 20th century figure drawing will be thoroughly discussed.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 ) and ( ART 2502 , ART 2504 , ART 2507 , or ART 2508 )

courses.title: Advanced Painting: Rome
courses.description: This course emphasizes the development of an active and reflective studio practice combined with the Rome experience. As the semester progresses, students identify and pursue their own projects, working independently with a collective critical structure with an emphasis on the development of a student's individual point of view. Experimentation is encouraged and there are frequent class critiques. Individual studios are provided.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2501 or ART 2503 )

courses.title: Fresco Painting
courses.description: This studio art course is designed to give students an overview of fresco painting techniques as practiced in Italy from the Roman through the Renaissance periods. While this is a studio art course, we will use the resources of Rome's churches and museums to understand the physical and symbolic structure of fresco painting throughout history from domestic to sacred spaces. Stylistic influences will be examined to create a coherent and correct wall painting using the same materials and techniques used by craftspeople of antiquity. As part of this course students will take a weekend excursion outside of Rome to participate in completing a permanent fresco. This course is open to beginning and advanced students.

courses.title: Comics: Sequential Narratives
courses.description: A course for intermediate and advanced drawing students exploring historical and contemporary issues in drawing through the narrative of the graphic novel. Studio work is complemented by an in-depth study of illustration, and imagination. After guided assignments, ultimate emphasis will be on self-directed projects that will be combined into a Graphic Novel.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 1503 .

courses.title: Color Photography I
courses.description: An introduction to basic skills in color photography. This course includes camera work and understanding of light, processing and printing with an emphasis on color theory, the development of personal imagery and the history of color photography.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2601 , PHOT 2441 , or GAD 2441 )

courses.title: View Camera
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to large format photography using a 4x5 view camera. Basic camera operation, various functions, specific uses, and potential as a creative tool are studied. A variety of specific exercises lead the student to proficient use of the view camera. Emphasis is on creative use as well as technical development. NOTE: Open to Photo majors only - special authorization required for non-majors.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 3603 , PHOT 3412 , or GAD 3412 )

courses.title: Darkroom Photography
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental vocabulary and techniques of darkroom photography. Skills of perception, visual competence, and black and white film-based photographic practice will be emphasized with an introduction to digital and darkroom hybrid techniques. Projects will address technical development as well as the development of personal vision through the photographic medium. Prior to fall 2016, the course title was "Photography II."

courses.title: Photographic Lighting
courses.description: At the core of any commercial or fine art photographer's practice is an in-depth understanding of lighting. This course is a thorough investigation of artificial lighting techniques (strobe and continuous) both in the studio and on location. Additional topics include advanced methods of exposure and the different approaches required in lighting for digital and film based images. A final portfolio is required. This course is repeatable for credit.

courses.title: Darkroom Photography
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the historic methods and materials of pre-digital black and white darkroom photography on location in Rome. Students will become familiar with Italian culture and with the techniques they are using to capture it deepening their understanding of the city and the creative process. Along with photo field trips the class will consist of lectures, demonstrations and group discussions. Weekly assignments will be given and a final portfolio of silver gelatin prints will be completed by the end of the semester. Images will be printed from negatives produced during the course. NOTE: Students are strongly encouraged to bring their own 35mm camera. A small number of basic film cameras will be available for limited student use.

courses.title: Digital Projects
courses.description: The emphasis of this course will be on creating a professional digital portfolio. Throughout the semester, students will learn a series of multimedia software applications and develop interactive presentations that will promote themselves as artists with contemporary and professional portfolios. NOTE: The course is limited to seniors and graduate students.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2602 , PHOT 2461 , or GAD 2461 )

courses.title: Contemporary Photography
courses.description: We live in an extraordinary moment in the history of photography, a moment much hoped for and anticipated by many champions of the medium. Finally one can say without qualification that photography is a medium fully embraced by the contemporary art world. While there has always been a movement to look at and discuss photography as art, photography has never played a more central, critical and vital role in contemporary art then it does now. This course will look at both the role that photography plays in contemporary art and the role that contemporary art plays in photography. By surveying contemporary trends in photography, students in this class will develop an understanding of what exactly photography is now. At the same time the class will attempt to answer questions about what it means to be contemporary, about what the relationship between the contemporary and the historical is, and why this might be important. Through these problems students will be encouraged to develop personal work that addresses themes and ideas discussed in the class. NOTE: Open to Junior/Seniors. Special authorization required for non-majors.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2601 , ART 2603 , PHOT 2441 , PHOT 2451 , GAD 2441 , or GAD 2451 )

courses.title: Color Photography I
courses.description: An introduction to basic skills in color processing and printing with an emphasis on development of personal imagery and the history of color picture making.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2601 , PHOT 2441 , or GAD 2441 )

courses.title: Special Topics in Photography
courses.description: This course explores special topics in photographic and imaging practices including new and emerging methods of research and production. Special topics courses can include lectures, demonstrations, readings, and student presentations in support of field and studio research. Both individual and collaborative practices may be addressed.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2601 , ART 2602 , ART 2901 , ART 2604 , ART 1602 , PHOT 2441 , PHOT 2461 , PHOT 2961 , PHOT 2401 , GAD 2441 , GAD 2461 , GAD 2961 , GAD 2401 , ARTU 2811 , PHOT 2811 , ARCH 1011 , or ARCH 1017 )

courses.title: Darkroom Photography II
courses.description: A continuation of advanced black and white photography with an introduction to the zone system and a variety of professional techniques. Emphasis will be on the development of a professional portfolio, classical black and white photographic history, and focused development of personal vision. Digital photographic techniques may also be included. Prior to Fall 2025, this course was titled "Advanced Photo Workshop."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( PHOT 2441 , PHOT 2451 , ART 2601 , ART 2603 , GAD 2441 , or GAD 2451 ) and ( ART 3603 , PHOT 3412 , or GAD 3412 )

courses.title: Alternative Photographic Processes
courses.description: This course is a survey covering a wide range of experimental and historical photographic processes that extend beyond traditional silver printing. Workshop orientation emphasizes a diverse exposure to many creative possibilities from hand applied photographic emulsions to artists' book production, culminating in a professional final project.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( PHOT 2441 , PHOT 2451 , ART 2601 , ART 2603 , GAD 2441 , or GAD 2451 ) and ( PHOT 3412 , ART 3603 , or GAD 3412 )

courses.title: Digital Photography II
courses.description: Digital Photography II explores advanced applications in digital imaging with an emphasis on photographic output. Emphasis will be placed on more sophisticated methods of capture and production including large format printing, advanced color management, cataloging, and archival storage practices. The development of a personal vision and lines of inquiry will be central. A professional portfolio will be required.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2601 , ART 2603 , PHOT 2441 , PHOT 2451 , GAD 2441 , or GAD 2451 )

courses.title: The Photo Book: Making and Understanding
courses.description: Throughout photography's history various artists have used the photo book to reach a wider audience, hone their voice, and give others a more personal experience of their work. In this course students will practice the technical and conceptual skills involved in crafting their own photo books while learning the history and criticisms of artists books. Students will learn how to edit, sequence, title and bind their own photo books using pictures or projects they may have already conceptualized. Tutorials, lectures, and critiques structure the class periods.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2601 , ART 2602 , ART 2901 , ART 2604 , ART 1603 , ART 1604 , or ART 1602 )

courses.title: Printmaking Workshop
courses.description: Print workshop is an all-print media print class intended for advanced print students developing their thesis work. Students should have advanced abilities in more than one printmaking process. This course is organized around working across print media, developing good project management skills, creating an ambitious body of artwork, and developing a sustainable practice for life after graduation. We will be investigating the ways the print and the multiple have become pervasive elements throughout the contemporary art world. We will be looking at a variety of sources and supporting materials that explore a gamut of working methods, ranging from traditional image creation to more experimental and new media methods that utilize print.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C in ( ART 1701 , ART 1702 , ART 2701 , ART 2702 , ART 2708 , or ART 2709 ), ( ART 2704 , ART 2705 , ART 2707 , ART 2711 , ART 2703 , or ART 2745 ), and ( ART 3702 , ART 3704 , ART 3705 , ART 3706 , or ART 3707 )

courses.title: Advanced Relief Printmaking
courses.description: This course builds on the students' working knowledge of relief printmaking. Students will explore contemporary methods of utilizing relief in a fine art context, including monoprint, digital tools, installation, publication, public art, and protest graphics. While engaging with the history and context of relief printmaking over the centuries, students will develop their own creative vision and unique portfolio of prints. NOTE: Prior to Fall 2026, this course was titled "Relief and Monoprint Workshop."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2711 and ART 2701 .

courses.title: Print in the Expanded Field
courses.description: This is a creative critical course for printmaking students interested in exploring the medium as a tool for conceptual inquiry. We will be investigating new questions in print media. Faculty and students explore the implications of current topics and the way historic and cultural context impacts contemporary creative practice today. The semester will include building off existing printmaking experience, which will be directly informed by reading and discussions, as well as experimental approaches of production, like t-shirt printing, rubber stamps, or meme production. Students will also consider different modes of distribution and audience engagement. Exact topics and processes covered will be determined by the professor teaching the course. NOTE: Prior to Fall 2026, this course was titled "Color Print Workshop."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2701 , ART 2702 , ART 2708 , or ART 2709 ) and ( ART 2703 , ART 2704 , ART 2705 , ART 2707 , or ART 2711 )

courses.title: Advanced Screen Printing
courses.description: This course will build on student's working knowledge of the process and history of screen printing, which has the distinction of being both one of the oldest printmaking processes and one of the most vital in contemporary art. This class is designed to allow students the freedom to explore their personal vision while further developing their proficiency with the medium. We will look at and respond to artists who are pushing the boundaries of the process and working in the "expanded field". We will be utilizing hand-drawn, photographic, and digitally manipulated source material. We will be learning and discussing modern techniques for constructing a printed image and printing large scale imagery. NOTE: Prior to Fall 2026, this course was titled "Advanced Serigraphy."
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2704 .

courses.title: Advanced Etching
courses.description: This course will build on students' basic working knowledge of the process and history of etching. Etching, or Intaglio, has the distinction of being a holistic product of the European Enlightenment, emerging from innovations in craft, politics, science, and economics, while also bearing direct and obvious connections to global indigenous practices of engraving and relief carving dating back to tens of thousands of years. Course projects will introduce students to advance techniques including multi-plate color printing, chine colle, spit-bite, softground, experimental methods, as well as laser and CNC engraving. Advanced students will develop their own unique creative vision in community with their peers.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2705 .

courses.title: Advanced Lithography
courses.description: This course is designed to develop the students' technical skills and their personal vision through the use of lithographic processes. Study will include stone lithography, plate lithography, color printing, and photo processes. This course will build your working knowledge of the process and history of lithography. The class is organized around themed assignments, which are designed to allow you to build your skills in the medium while continuing to develop your personal vision and research practices.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2707 , PRNT 2751, PRNT 2761, GAD 2751 , or GAD 2761 )

courses.title: Advanced Artists' Books
courses.description: This course is for advanced exploration of artists' books. Students will learn to make a new, more complex book form, while continuing to explore the book as a mode of creative and conceptual self-expression. Students will further explore the history and context of book arts and artist's books and develop their own creative voice in the form. Processes explored will include binding, box-making, and letterpress, and students will also consider different modes of distribution.

courses.title: Art Career Workshop
courses.description: Creative and practical solutions to career problems of the artist; preparation of the art student for postgraduate challenges.

courses.title: Advanced Video
courses.description: This course is geared towards students who are working with concepts best expressed through the various forms of video art. Projects will develop and challenge the students' ability to address technical, formal, and conceptual elements in their work. NOTE: Students are expected to have some prior knowledge of video production and/or postproduction.

courses.title: Installation
courses.description: Investigations into the intrinsic meaning of the site will be coupled with the effective channeling of those issues into the work of art. Ideas, material, and placement will be analyzed so as to achieve cogent integration into the site. Introduction to use of scale models and various types of models to analyze a site and plan work for a site is part of this course. Lectures, individual discussions, and group critiques are scheduled.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Mold Making Technology
courses.description: Flexible moldmaking techniques are explored using foam, latex, RTV and silicone rubber, as well as alginate compounds for direct body casts. Non-flexible techniques include wood forms for cement castings. Positives are cast in cement, plaster, rubber and polyurethane using both solid and hollow casting methods. Students incorporate these techniques in directed projects, or for completing self-directed work.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Advanced Sculpture
courses.description: Emphasis on development of an individual direction in sculpture through studio work, drawing, writing, and some research. Progress is reviewed through individual critiques. The development of critical analysis of completed work is emphasized in group critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 , ART 2807 , PDS 2611 , PDS 2621 , SCLP 2611, or SCLP 2621)

courses.title: Advanced Sculpture
courses.description: Emphasis on development of an individual direction in sculpture through studio work, drawing, writing, and some research. Progress is reviewed through individual critiques. The development of critical analysis of completed work is emphasized in group critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Advanced Sculpture
courses.description: Emphasis on development of an individual direction in sculpture through studio work and special research on topics relative to contemporary practice. Progress is reviewed through individual critiques. The development of critical analysis of completed work is emphasized in group critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 , ART 2807 , SCLP 2611, SCLP 2621, PDS 2611 , or PDS 2621 )

courses.title: Advanced Sculpture
courses.description: Emphasis on development of an individual direction in sculpture through studio work, drawing, writing, and some research. Progress is reviewed through individual critiques. The development of critical analysis of completed work is emphasized in group critiques.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Public Art Projects
courses.description: The class will introduce the processes involved in designing actual site-specific public art projects. These will include site research, design development, architectural drawings and model building, and presentation techniques. Studio visits with architects, model-makers, sculptors, and project coordinators are an integral part of the course. Students work on an actual project that is juried by area arts professionals at the end of the semester. NOTE: Special authorization is required from the instructor in order to register for this class.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Sculpture Techniques and Materials
courses.description: This course is meant to give students the tools they need to acquire and produce and exhibit. Students will examine displays in multiple contexts, and will be introduced to presentation concepts in art, retail, and the home. They will gain skills in exhibit design, model-making, proper art handling, crate design, fabrication, and shipping. The course will culminate with an off-campus exhibit that is themed, designed, installed and publicized by the class. NOTE: Special authorization for all.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 or ART 2807 )

courses.title: Foundry
courses.description: Ceramic shell bronze and aluminum casting techniques are emphasized, as well as a variety of hot and cold casting materials and processes. The course focuses on the way these techniques serve sculptural thinking. NOTE: Special authorization for all.

courses.title: Junior Sculpture Seminar
courses.description: This studio class is a bridge from lower level introductory courses to advanced studio work. Aspirations of the profession, studio principles, and critical thinking are stressed, along with readings and discussions in contemporary art theory.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( ART 2801 , ART 2807 , SCLP 2611, SCLP 2621, PDS 2611 , or PDS 2621 )

courses.title: Sculpture Workshop
courses.description: The main focus of the course will be to help each student develop a well-considered and professional show of their own work.

courses.title: Public of One, Public of Many
courses.description: What do we mean by the word public? General public? A public? The public? Or its plural, publics? In this course students create a range of works - objects, installations, actions, interventions, participatory events, and situations for varying publics. These will include works for an intimate audience of one (which is a public), our class (another public), our Tyler colleagues, the Temple community, and the City of Philadelphia. What questions should we ask to create works for these varying publics? Through an exploratory curriculum, students construct these questions and instigate inventive and meaningful responses.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ( FDPR 1511 (may be taken concurrently) or FDPR 1512 (may be taken concurrently)) and FDPR 1531 .

courses.title: Puppetry
courses.description: Take a look around you. Our world is built out of static objects that IF enacted upon, have the potential for movement, bringing static forms to life. If this is true, then everything can be a puppet! However, not everything can be an engaging and expressive puppet. When designing objects for performance, attention to functionality is key to creating engaging, transformative objects. In this course, students will receive an overview of the contemporary puppetry landscape with an emphasis on design for performance and how everything can be alive! Through solo and group work, students will build wooden marionettes, explore projection as performance, and delve into the world of found object puppetry. Please note that we will not be covering hand and rod puppets (foam and felt or "Muppet"-like puppets). Students will leave the class with a grounding in historic and contemporary puppetry and the conceptual and technical experience to generate exciting and meaningful engagements through the language of puppetry.

courses.title: Art/Work
courses.description: This is a seminar about art and work, as well as art as a form of work. Students will investigate their practice as a profession in relation to other forms of labor and to artists who critically explore conventional and innovative forms of actively engaging in the making of images and objects, knowledge and experience. The course will collectively produce a resource guide to being a working artist today. Note: Prior to Fall 2024, this course was titled "PDS Seminar."

courses.title: BFA Senior Thesis: Exhibition and Installation
courses.description: This course serves as a capstone of the BFA curriculum, focusing on the development and execution of a solo Senior thesis exhibition. It emphasizes both the formal aspects of installation and exhibition design and the conceptual and curatorial strategies essential to organizing a cohesive exhibition. You will engage in a meaningful, collaborative exercise involving the critical and practical aspects of curating a group exhibition; this may take the form of organizing a group exhibition, or something similar. Students will explore techniques for conceptualizing and designing successful solo and group exhibitions. Throughout the semester, discussion and critique will play a central role, offering students valuable support and feedback. Additionally, students will draft a comprehensive thesis document to provide context and critical insight into their body of work. To further prepare for their careers as professional artists, students will also focus on archiving and documenting their work, ensuring that their exhibition continues to serve them beyond their time at Tyler.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 4097 and ART 3053 .

courses.title: BFA Senior Thesis: Publication and Distribution
courses.description: This course serves as the capstone of the BFA curriculum, focusing on the development and production of a body of creative work. This course emphasizes engagement with the broad histories of publishing and distribution, artist's multiples, zines, artist's book, and other creative forms which derive meaning from similar traditions. Students will explore and design successful models of production, public events planning, and modes of distribution. Throughout the semester, discussion and feedback will play a central role. Additionally, students will draft a comprehensive thesis document to provide context and critical insight into their body of work. To further prepare for their careers as professional artists, students will also focus on archiving and documenting their work, ensuring that their creative work continues to serve them beyond their time at Tyler.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 4097 and ART 3053 .

courses.title: BFA Senior Thesis: Utility and Production
courses.description: This course serves as the capstone of the BFA curriculum, focusing on the development and production of a body of creative work. This section focuses on the design process and utility as a creative practice to investigate a range of production means for a given object/outcome. This class will explore contemporary design through a critical lens. Throughout the semester, discussion and feedback will play a central role. Additionally, students will draft a comprehensive thesis document to provide context and critical insight into their body of work. To further prepare for their careers as professional artists, students will also focus on archiving and documenting their work, ensuring that their creative work continues to serve them beyond their time at Tyler.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 4097 and ART 3053 .

courses.title: BFA Senior Thesis: Performance and Event
courses.description: This course serves as the capstone of the BFA curriculum, focusing on the development and production of a body of creative work. This course emphasizes engagement with the broad histories of new media art, including, time-based, video, animation, performance, and art events, and other creative forms which derive meaning from similar traditions. Students will explore and design successful models of production, public events planning, and modes of distribution. Throughout the semester, discussion and feedback will play a central role. Additionally, students will draft a comprehensive thesis document to provide context and critical insight into their body of work. To further prepare for their careers as professional artists, students will also focus on archiving and documenting their work, ensuring that their creative work continues to serve them beyond their time at Tyler.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 4097 and ART 3053 .

courses.title: Time, Art and Tech Senior Studio
courses.description: In Senior Studio, students focus on developing a rigorous and well-defined, independent studio practice. This course is designed to engage students' understanding of artistic approaches, technical, and spatial realization. To that end, we begin by identifying the breadth of what research is, the forms studio and post-studio practice can take, and how experimentation is key. Student work will combine technical experimentation with well-researched content in projects that are ready for installation and/or exhibition. The course will foster critical thinking, particularly with a focus on fine-tuning one's central concerns while producing a cohesive body of work. As such, students will be able to reflect on content, overall methodology, as well as to contextualize and communicate the work within contemporary cultural frames. Students receive ongoing feedback through individual and group critiques. The final artworks will be shown at an end-of-semester presentation, where students will be able to learn with and from reviewers interacting with their works.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2062 , ART 2063 , ART 2064 , and ART 3063 .

courses.title: Senior Thesis Writing Time and Technology
courses.description: As artists, we have the opportunity and burden to communicate our ideas through language. In support of the fact that the artistic process is more than what is exhibited, this course provides a structure for writing a thesis paper that formalizes the background research, histories, and contexts for their individually driven artworks. Students will examine artists', curators' and critics' texts, complete a series of writing assignments, and engage in class discussions, to develop a body of written work that through the editing process, becomes the thesis paper. While this course will supply the necessary tools to write a solid thesis paper and speak articulately about one's work, we will also examine other artists' use of language to see how we might produce beyond the visual.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2062 , ART 2063 , ART 2064 , and ART 3063 .

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Self-directed study and research for upper-level BFA students developed in conjunction with, and supervised by, a full-time faculty member in the major area of the student.

courses.title: Professional Practices in Art
courses.description: Covers many aspects of career, business and professional practices as they relate to a range of contemporary modes of artistic production. The course includes information and resources relating to artist residencies, grants, internships, and jobs. Business-oriented topics include the pricing of work, taxes, contracts, bookkeeping for small businesses, marketing, legal problems, insurance, advertising, and publicity, artist-gallery relations, and studio operations. NOTE: This is a writing intensive course. Prior to fall 2023, the course title was "Professional Practices in Crafts."

courses.title: Art in Practice
courses.description: Art in Practice offers creative and practical skills for art students' post-graduation in building an ongoing practice, a sustainable livelihood, and a supportive creative community. Through guest lectures, field trips, writing, individual meetings, peer review and presentations, students are exposed to a multitude of ways to sustain a creative life and career. As a writing intensive course, students develop their writing and communication skills in order to express their concepts clearly and develop their written personal creative voice. Students will leave the course with a packet of professional materials after exploring topics like making an artist's presentation, resume preparation, writing an artist's statement, writing an artist bio, writing a grant, applying for artist residencies, and other career opportunities. This work will be contextualized within conversations of the individual and social labor of art within contemporary communities, exploring themes of labor, autonomy, ownership, organizing, and art economies.

courses.title: Advanced Ceramics II
courses.description: Problems in ceramics for the advanced student with emphasis on individual research projects with emphasis upon portfolio development.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in 6 credits in ART 3101 .
prereq_notes: Non-course prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in 6 credits in ART 3101 .

courses.title: Senior Ceramics
courses.description: Fourth-year concentration in ceramics and thesis work.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in 6 credits in ART 3101 .
prereq_notes: Non-course prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in 6 credits in ART 3101 .

courses.title: Threading the Needle: Drawing with Stitch II
courses.description: This class builds on techniques learned in Stitching I and includes a research component alongside the development of a studio practice. Students will create a proposal for their research and studio projects that will focus on involved projects that incorporate intermediate and more advanced techniques in the area. Faculty will work individually with students to develop their work, teaching them specific techniques relevant to their stated projects. Students will be expected to present their work to the department and be able to talk about their work and research.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 3201 .

courses.title: Dyeing for Color II
courses.description: This class allows students to further develop their work and research in dyeing and related processes through introducing intermediate and more advanced techniques; working independently students are able to pursue specific areas and projects.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2201 and ART 2202 .

courses.title: Jacquard II
courses.description: This class allows students to further develop their work and research with the Jacquard Loom through introducing intermediate and more advanced techniques; working independently students are able to pursue specific areas and projects.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 3208 .

courses.title: Woven Structure III
courses.description: An exploration of advanced weaving techniques: computer loom drafting and weaving, three-dimensional investigations and structural manipulations.
courses.prereq_text: Minimum grade of C- in ART 2204 and ART 3204 .

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Fibers and Material Studies
courses.description: Seniors work independently on research and making work that addresses their individual interests within a contemporary art context.
